title: Skyline Payments - Integration Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer primarily cares about PCI scope, gateway/proxy setup, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, rate limiting, and observability hooks. Agreed to run a small pilot with sample traffic and share security docs and pricing for Dedicated/private sizing.
next_steps: Redwood to send Dedicated and Private pricing and sizing worksheet
Share SOC2 and network diagrams with Ethan
Schedule a 2-hour technical deep dive/benchmarks session with Priya and SEs next week
Start 2-week pilot using Redwood Hosted sandbox with sample traffic
action_items: Maya Chen: Send Dedicated pricing + sizing spreadsheet (due 2026-10-09)
Samir Patel: Prepare benchmark template and list of sample prompts for pilot (due 2026-10-08)
Ethan Brooks: Share PCI scoping questions and existing card-flow diagram (due 2026-10-08)
Priya Singh: Provide example query mix and peak RPS estimates (due 2026-10-07)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-06 16:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jared Morales (CTO, Skyline), Priya Singh (Sr Engineer), Lila Gomez (Head of Platform), Ethan Brooks (Security)

00:00 Jared: okay everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. we wanted to run through how you guys see integrations working with redwood — specifically around SDKs and our gateway layer.
00:12 Maya: thanks jared. quick agenda, we'll do intros, current infra/constraints, integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), SDKs and langchain/llamaindex support, rate limits and quota model, observability hooks, then next steps. does that sound good?
00:25 Jared: yes sounds good. background: we are a payments platform, most of our user flows touch card data, so PCI scope is front and center. we currently run most inference in house for a couple microservices but exploring bringing some features external, especially for customer support assistant and fraud triage.
00:43 Priya: technical stack: python microservices, heavy use of LangChain and LlamaIndex for retrieval augmented generation. vector store is FAISS right now, but we host it in k8s. traffic for the assistant is spiky, typical peak about 120 rps for short prompts, average prompt length small, but reranking and embeddings jobs are heavier.
01:05 Samir: got it. quick q on embeddings — are you batching them client side or centralizing?
01:10 Priya: currently batching on a worker pool; we send batches of ~64 for production embeddings jobs.
01:15 Olivia: perfect, that maps well to some of our batching recommendations. on the integration side, do you prefer SDK usage directly from your services, or do you want a gateway/proxy in front of redwood?
01:27 Lila: our SRE prefers gateway so we can centralize auth and rate limits, plus easier telemetry. but we are open to direct SDK calls if that reduces hops.
01:36 Maya: two common patterns: 1) app services call Redwood SDK directly with API keys (fastest path), 2) internal gateway/proxy which handles auth, quotas, routing (gives you central control). For PCI, many customers choose Dedicated or Private to keep card flows out of public hosted logs.
01:53 Ethan: question: if we use Hosted, how is card data handled? are there recommended patterns to avoid putting PANs into prompts?
02:00 Maya: good question — we strongly recommend tokenization or redaction before sending user data. Hosted has data retention controls and contractual protections, but for full PCI-compliant isolation we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll share the exact KMS/hsm options in the security pack.
02:12 Jared: can you support language-specific SDKs? we have python and a small node service.
02:18 Maya: yes we have official python and node SDKs, plus REST. we also have examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors. Samir, do you want to demo the LangChain flow?
02:26 Samir: sure, brief overview: you can swap our client into the LangChain LLM wrapper — code is essentially a small adapter. there are some quirks: streaming support maps to langchain callbacks, retrieval plugins for LlamaIndex work with our response structures too though occasionally names get slightly different — like we used to see munged model names in older clients.
02:46 Priya: that's helpful. latency is a big one for us; our SLA to customers is 200ms P95 for the support assistant. can Redwood hit that on hosted?
02:55 Samir: short answer: depends on model and sequence length. for small prompts using optimized model variants and streaming, many Hosted customers see sub-200ms for p95 on short sequences. We also have Dedicated pools you can pin to guarantee capacity — that improves latency predictability.
03:12 Priya: okay, and how do rate limits/quotas work? we want per-team quotas and token limits. also need to throttle reranking jobs differently.
03:21 Maya: platform supports per-api-key quotas and rate limits. For Dedicated we integrate with your internal auth too. You can set per-route quotas and custom throttling windows. We also support burst capacity rules.
03:34 Lila: can we put a proxy in front and still get per-user telemetry back in Redwood Console? we want token-level cost breakdowns per internal team.
03:42 Olivia: yes — if you forward identity headers from your gateway we can preserve token attribution in the console. Alternatively, use per-service API keys and map back to teams.
03:50 Jared: on observability, we need tracing hooks — span correlation to our existing tracing (we use Jaeger/OpenTelemetry).
03:58 Samir: we provide traceId propagation header and an SDK hook to attach spans. Also export logs to your SIEM or to our Console which has per-route charts. There is a small sampling agent for request-level full traces to save cost.
04:15 Priya: great. what about LlamaIndex specifics — we have a lot of fetch/loader code and want to avoid rewriting. any adapter examples?
04:22 Samir: yes we have a LlamaIndex connector in our examples repo. It shows the retriever and indexer calls and how to hook in streaming and the message format. Small note: some indexer fields are named slightly differently in our payloads; our README calls those out.
04:36 Priya: can you support FAISS and vector embeddings format compatibility?
04:41 Olivia: embeddings output is standard float vectors, and we provide an on-boarding script to convert to common formats. For FAISS it's straightforward; we also provide recommended quantization for cost.
04:51 Ethan: security again — KMS integration, customer-managed keys?
04:55 Maya: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS, HSM options. Hosted supports KMS with contractual key controls and restricted access, but for full key control we recommend Private. We'll include the KMS integration docs in the pack.
05:07 Lila: network topology — if we go Dedicated, can we have VPC peering or is it a VPN?
05:12 Maya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link depending on cloud. Private can be fully customer-hosted on-prem or in your VPC. We'll need to map exact cloud accounts.
05:21 Jared: latency concerns for the fraud triage — those are heavier models and longer sequences. Do you recommend batching there or separate Dedicated pool?
05:28 Samir: often we recommend a mixed approach: Dedicated pool for low-latency short prompts and a separate batch/async pool for heavy reranking or embeddings. Our routing can auto-fallback if capacity is constrained.
05:41 Priya: curious about cost model — per-token pricing for Hosted, how does Dedicated work? flat commit + usage?
05:47 Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity: monthly commit for GPU pools plus usage tiers. We provide guidance to pick GPU type and pool size based on your RPS and sequence distribution.
05:58 Jared: do you have any known PCI customers in payments who used Hosted safely? or is everyone going Dedicated?
06:05 Maya: some customers use Hosted with strict redaction/tokenization and contracts, but many payments customers choose Dedicated or Private to reduce scope of PCI. we'll share references and case studies where allowed.
06:17 Priya: can we test the SDK integration quickly? say a small sandbox token and a short demo using our LangChain pipeline?
06:22 Maya: absolutely. we can provision a sandbox hosted key and a small test model. Samir will share a repo with LangChain and LlamaIndex runnable examples tailored to your stack.
06:31 Samir: i'll also include a local proxy example that you can drop in front of your services; shows how to preserve trace headers and do rate-limit enforcement.
06:39 Lila: about quotas — can we set different token caps for different environments (staging vs prod)?
06:44 Olivia: yes you can. We typically recommend separate API keys per environment, then attach billing and quota policies.
06:51 Ethan: is there support for long-term audit logs? we need 12 months of request logs retained for compliance.
06:57 Maya: audit log retention is part of our enterprise add-ons. Dedicated and Private options allow longer retention. Hosted has default retention windows but we can extend for a fee.
07:07 Priya: do you do model quantization recommendations? for embeddings we want to trade off accuracy and cost.
07:13 Samir: yes our Optimize team provides quantization and model recommendations based on workload. We'll run sample benchmarks as part of the pilot to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
07:24 Jared: what about failover — if a Dedicated pool is saturated, can we fall back to hosted?
07:29 Maya: yes we can set fallback policies to compatible model variants in Hosted. You can also do canary rollouts.
07:36 Priya: curious about SDK behavior on network retries — do you expose circuit-breaker hooks?
07:41 Samir: SDK includes retry/backoff settings and a circuit-breaker hook. For gateway setups, we recommend implementing token buckets at the gateway as well.
07:50 Lila: do you have example configs for k8s sidecars or envoy filters for the proxy pattern?
07:55 Olivia: yes samples for envoy and k8s sidecar are in the repo I'll share. They include rate limit configs and header mappings.
08:05 Ethan: we will need a threat model review — i'll take that offline but want to flag the need.
08:11 Maya: perfect, please send your questions and we'll loop in security.
08:15 Jared: ok let's talk pilot scope. Priya, what would you consider success?
08:20 Priya: if we can integrate LangChain pipeline, hit our latency targets at 80% of traffic, and show cost estimates per 100k requests, that's success. Also demonstrate telemetry mapping to our teams.
08:30 Maya: sounds good. proposal: Redwood provisions hosted sandbox for integration and a small Dedicated sizing doc. We'll run a 2-week pilot with sample traffic you provide. At the end, share latency/cost report and next-step pricing for Dedicated/Private.
08:44 Jared: timeline? we want to decide by end of month.
08:47 Maya: we can get the sandbox and artifacts out in 48-72 hours, deep-dive next week, and pilot can start once we finalize sample workloads.
08:56 Priya: ok works. one more: do you provide a proxy that can do per-tenant routing so we can split internal customers across different model variants?
09:05 Samir: yes, routing rules allow per-tenant model selection and canary percentages. That is part of the gateway pattern.
09:14 Lila: any upfront infra changes required for us for Private?
09:18 Maya: Private usually needs some coordination (network, infra account access if cloud-hosted), but we provide an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. We'll outline requirements in the security/network doc.
09:30 Jared: thanks everyone, let's recap action items and next steps.
09:35 Maya: recap: we'll send pricing/sizing, security pack, example repos for LangChain/LlamaIndex, envoy sidecar samples, and schedule the deep dive. Samir/Olivia to own the technical repo share.
09:46 Jared: thanks, appreciate it.
09:50 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings, e.g., "pan" for PAN, "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes mis-transcribed as "Redwood dedicate". Some timestamps are approximate. Shared artifacts: link: /redwood/repos/langchain-llamaindex-examples, link: /redwood/security/soc2-kms-pack, link: /redwood/pricing/dedicated-sizing.xlsx
